text:
maya: Heads up — seeing an unexpected spike in credits. After the pricing-experiment rollback last night a backfill job appears to have issued auto-reverse credits for ~120 customers.
maya: Stripe shows ~120 credit memos (credit_note.created) but NetSuite has *no* matching credit memos imported, causing account mismatch and negative receivables on the ledger.
alex: Can you paste an example event/id and the job run id? Also which backfill did we run (batch vs streaming)?
maya: Job: billing-backfill-2026-03-22-23. Payload sample from logs:
```
{ "event": "credit_note.created", "data": { "object": { "id": "cn_1JX...", "invoice": "in_1IX...", "lines": [...] } }, "metadata": { "backfill_job": "billing-backfill-2026-03-22-23" } }
```
maya: Notice there is no idempotency_key in the log; and the backfill was retried several times by the queue.
liam: My hunch: the backfill workers didn't attach an idempotency key and the queue fanout retried the same invoice multiple times across workers -> duplicate credit creation race. Also NetSuite importer expects a `source_id` mapping and maybe filtered by a job tag; if the importer only applied when `source=webhook` it missed these backfill-created credits.
stripe-bot: automatic: processed events: credit_note.created x120 (batch=bf-2026-03-22)
sam: Customers have started pinging CS — a few reported unexpected statement credits. We should pause the batch and prepare comms.
nina: Finance hold: do not apply manual reversals yet. We need an extract of affected customers + amounts so we can quantify revenue impact before any corrective posting.
alex: On it. I'll pause the backfill: kubectl scale deployment billing-backfill --replicas=0 -n prod and pause the queue in SQS (set VisibilityTimeout high) until we triage.
liam: Quick patch idea: treat invoice id as idempotency key and reject credit creation if a credit_note already exists for that invoice in stripe metadata. I'll open a PR to add idempotency header to credit-note creation calls.
alex: I can run a dedupe script to reconcile Stripe <> NetSuite: export stripe credit_notes with metadata.backfill_job=bf-2026-03-22, then match to NetSuite imports; produce CSV for nina. I'll also check whether NetSuite import logs rejected entries and surface the reason (mapping/missing field).
maya: Sample query I'll need from Alex: SELECT customer_id, invoice_id, credit_note_id, amount, created_at FROM stripe_credit_notes WHERE metadata->>'backfill_job' = 'bf-2026-03-22';
alex: Got it — will run and upload CSV to finance-drive in ~20m.
liam: Also adding a short-term mitigation: add a distributed lock on invoice id for the backfill worker so only a single worker can process a given invoice at a time. Long term: idempotency keys + recorder in DB.
sam: For comms: can someone draft a one-paragraph explanation and impacted count so CS can reply with a timeframe?
maya: I'll draft a message once we have the CSV. Nina, do you want to approve any immediate refunds reversal or wait for reconciliation?
nina: Wait — finance needs the CSV first. If NetSuite didn't import the credit memos, we may need to re-ingest them rather than issue refunds. Hold on manual adjustments.
alex: Action items: 1) I paused deployment and queue; 2) run export (CSV) and post; 3) check NetSuite import errors. liam: Action items: open PR for idempotency/lock and staging test. maya: I'll coordinate CS message draft after CSV lands.
maya: Thanks — marking this high priority. If anyone sees customer-impacting refunds already processed, ping me directly.
alex: CSV uploaded: drive.redwood.com/finance/backfill_credit_flood_2026-03-22.csv :eyes:
sam: Received — starting templated replies for CS once we confirm numbers. :thumbsup:
nina: Thanks team. Please keep patches scoped and revertible. We'll reconvene in 30m after initial reconciliation.
